unlisted_practices: Document the purpose, design and update plans, modeling assumptions, prespecified simulation objectives, design adjustments, and simulation outcomes of a digital twin used to inform AI design decisions before each deployment.
Include a deployment lead, domain scientist, and data scientist on the design team of a digital twin used to evaluate AI decision-making algorithms.
Avoid data leakage when compiling prior data for simulation by splitting data into disjoint sets for simulation modeling and for prior or hyperparameter selection.
Avoid removing data representative of real-world deployments, such as disengaged participants, when building simulation models used to evaluate AI algorithms.
Construct variants of the base simulation testbed to test the robustness of candidate AI algorithms to incorrect modeling assumptions and imputed parameters.

Evaluate candidate AI decision-making algorithms in simulation with stochastic noise matching that observed in prior data, quantifying uncertainty with confidence intervals across repeated simulations.
Identify and address data-deployment mismatches, such as domain shift, sampling bias, and missing variables, between prior data and the upcoming deployment using sensitivity analyses.
Apply verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification iteratively to simulation models before using their results for design decisions.
Ensure replicable simulations by tracking random number generation seeds and sharing code, procedures, and data where possible.
Update the simulation model with data collected during each deployment to continually improve AI design decisions for subsequent deployments.
Make AI design decisions between deployments rather than during deployment to preserve intervention fidelity and replicability.
Select evaluation metrics for candidate AI algorithms according to intervention goals, including lower-percentile outcomes for least-benefited individuals and early-termination performance.

screen.reason: This is a framework/methodology perspective paper describing how digital twins can be used to simulate and optimize design decisions for just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs) rather than an empirical study testing a specific deployment practice.
